posts.body:
Thanks for the replies.
The line "const wx = (Graphics.boxWidth - windowWidth * 2) / 2; // Center horizontally" from picture1WindowRect() goes along with the line "    const wx = (Graphics.boxWidth + windowWidth * 2) / 2; // Center horizontally from picture2WindowRect() so those two are side by side centered horizontally.
I did have a look at this to double check however, and even removing the "*2" the windows still appeared just left of their supposed center alignment.
The lines:
// Calculate new dimensions for 95% scaling
const scaledWidth = bitmap.width * 0.95;
const scaledHeight = bitmap.height * 0.95;
Were done like that because putting it at 100 seems to be cutting of a bit from the right side of the pictures (*Those windows are 720x720, at 100% the pictures inside are 720x720).
This made me think it's a padding issue which brought me to...
I have sort of figure out a workaround but i'm worried it's gonna cause issues later down the line.
I now THINK it's some sort of padding issue, as my workaround involved basically adding "+8" to each window's individual x-values and it seems to have fixed it. But if that is the case, I'm unsure as to why there is padding to begin with, when:
a.) i've set default padding to "0" in my game.
b.) the windows are being drawn in a custom scene, so the x=values of the window should be defined by the edge of the GraphicsBox right?
I suppose you guys see it and experience all the time, but I am only recently learning how continously frustrating it is when you figure out all these elaborate code and functions and smash them out easy, only to get stuck on one tiny little thing like center alignment for what seems like an age.

posts.body:
Ray9unn said:
Those windows are 720x720, at 100% the pictures inside are 720x720
Click to expand...
The contents area of a window is smaller than the window itself. Are you perhaps adjusting the padding after the contents area has already been created? This would cause it to be smaller than intended.
And in general I'd recommend against dynamically scaling a picture like this, since it tends to look rather ugly. Just scale it in a graphics editor and render it at 100% in-game.
Ray9unn said:
a.) i've set default padding to "0" in my game.
Click to expand...
How exactly did you do that? I suspect whatever you've done here is slightly messing with things.
Just to confirm some things:
- If you draw a window at x=0, does its left edge touch the left edge of the screen?
- If you draw it at x=Graphics.width-windowWidth, does its right edge touch the right edge of the screen?
